stem: A project team records substantive decisions in a partner-controlled collaboration service. Its access ends when the contract closes, but the organization needs the decisions afterward. Which requirement should be established before closure?
choices: A local copy of final deliverables without the decisions and supporting attachments
A retention promise from the partner without a continuing organizational retrieval mechanism
An authorized export capturing required decisions, attachments, and usable context
A project index listing links while leaving all substantive content under expiring access
rationale: The organization needs usable decision evidence after access ends, so export requirements must include the relevant context and components. Partner retention without retrieval does not ensure availability, links cannot overcome expired access, and final deliverables alone may not explain decisions. The agreement must preserve what the organization actually requires.

stem: A payroll clerk regularly prints sensitive reports to a shared printer in an open reception area. Electronic access permissions are appropriate. Which control most directly reduces the exposed information at the point where the current safeguard ends?
choices: Require the clerk to confirm payroll access permissions before each print job
Log every print request but retain immediate unattended output at reception
Use controlled print release and secure handling of printed reports
Ask reception staff to move accumulated reports to payroll each afternoon
rationale: Controlled release and secure handling address exposure as printed information becomes available. Checking application permissions does not prevent other people reading output. Print logs support accountability but not physical protection. Afternoon collection leaves an exposure window during which visitors or unauthorized staff can access the reports.

stem: A booking service offers an optional public customer profile. Designers propose making profiles visible until customers find a settings page and opt out. Which redesign best applies privacy as the default while preserving the optional feature?
choices: Start profiles private and offer a clear deliberate sharing choice
Require customers to submit a support request before changing profile visibility
Keep profiles public and obtain consent through acceptance of general service terms
Start profiles public but automatically remove them after thirty days
rationale: A private starting state protects users automatically while preserving an informed choice to share. General service terms do not make public exposure a privacy-protective default. Later removal still permits initial exposure. A support request creates unnecessary friction and does not implement the intended default protection at registration.

stem: A project spans locations with only thirty minutes of overlapping work time. Decisions frequently stall because supporting evidence is presented for the first time during live meetings. What collaboration design best improves continuity?
choices: Email separate regional briefing packs and reconcile decisions after each regional meeting
Rotate meeting times and keep all evidence review dependent on live attendance
Use shared pre-read evidence and recorded decisions with asynchronous review
Require delegates in each region to approve content before seeing other regions' comments
rationale: Asynchronous access to shared evidence allows contributions across time zones, with one recorded decision context. Regional approval before seeing other input prevents genuine shared review. Rotating live sessions redistributes inconvenience without resolving limited overlap, while separate packs require repeated reconciliation and can fragment the authoritative discussion and outcome.

stem: Halfway through an IM initiative, the planned acquisition of a business unit is canceled, removing most projected transaction volume. The remaining solution is feasible but its original benefits no longer apply. What should the program owner take to the investment committee?
choices: An updated case comparing continuation, resizing, and stopping against revised benefits
A completion report focused on technical milestones already achieved
The original approved case because the project has already received authorization
A request to increase transaction estimates until the original return reappears
rationale: The business case supports decisions throughout the program and should incorporate material changes. Comparing viable options using revised benefits enables an informed investment decision. Original authorization does not validate obsolete assumptions. Technical progress alone omits value, and inflated transaction estimates would misrepresent the basis for continued investment.

stem: A supplier offers an inexpensive specialized authoring format with excellent design features. No other product can open it, and the documents must remain usable for twenty years. What requirement most directly addresses the resulting dependency?
choices: Demonstrate a tested export path preserving required document characteristics
Require a faster viewer for the current desktop environment
Negotiate additional author licenses for the current release
Obtain a larger storage allocation for native documents
rationale: A tested export path addresses dependence on one supplier and exposes which required characteristics survive conversion. Extra storage preserves bytes without access, a faster viewer improves current performance, and additional licenses expand current use without resolving future dependence on the proprietary format.

stem: An engineering partnership needs a joint workspace. Each partner can share project drawings, but unrelated customer designs must remain confidential. Which initial design best balances collaboration and the boundary requirement?
choices: Give partner accounts the same access as internal engineering staff
Create a scoped workspace with explicitly authorized partner access
Exchange complete engineering libraries through encrypted transfer packages
Let partners browse internal folders and request restricted files
rationale: A scoped workspace limits disclosure to approved project material while enabling direct collaboration. Internal-role equivalence may expose unrelated designs, browse-and-request can reveal confidential metadata, and encryption protects transfer but does not justify sending complete libraries. The sharing boundary must be designed before content is exposed.

stem: Several departments need consistent standards for configuring their content platform and a formal group of specialists to advise on difficult implementations. Which governance structure most directly fits this continuing requirement?
choices: A voluntary community of practice for informal experience sharing
A temporary incident team activated when information is exposed
A steering committee focused on strategic priorities and funding
A center of excellence with assigned specialist responsibilities
rationale: A center of excellence provides formal specialist leadership, standards, guidance, and reusable expertise. A community of practice supports voluntary learning rather than assigned standards ownership. An incident team addresses exceptional events. A steering committee makes strategic decisions but does not usually supply the detailed technical and process expertise described.

stem: A migration resets creation dates to import day. Fixed review workflows use the target's creation field; that field permits mapped historical values. Original dates are verified in the export. Ingestion time also matters for audit. Which remediation best preserves both meanings?
choices: Preserve historical dates in a sidecar export while allowing the workflow to use import time
Change every review rule to subtract a single average migration delay from creation
Keep import time as creation and add historical dates to an unstructured migration note
Map verified original dates to creation; retain import time in a separate ingestion field
rationale: Separate fields preserve both events and supply the existing workflow with the date it actually requires. Notes and sidecars retain evidence but do not fix workflow behavior. An average delay cannot reconstruct different historical dates accurately. Mapping should preserve meaning, rather than make import events stand in for document creation.

stem: A committee sends meeting packs as email attachments. Late corrections create several packs, and participants cannot determine which agenda contains the current supporting papers. Which replacement most directly fixes this failure?
choices: Publish one governed meeting workspace and email links to its current pack
Issue corrected packs with sequential filenames and ask recipients to delete earlier attachments
Freeze the first emailed pack and circulate corrections separately during the meeting
Continue attachments but have the chair maintain a private list of corrected versions
rationale: A governed common location directly resolves uncertainty about the current pack. Sequential filenames and deletion requests still depend on recipient reconciliation, a private version list does not provide participants a shared current source, and freezing an erroneous pack with separate corrections forces readers to assemble the applicable evidence themselves.

stem: A hospital can fund one initial process project. Medication authorization is safety critical and poorly understood; equipment requests are frequent, well documented, and delayed by repeated clerical checks. Leadership seeks a demonstrable improvement this quarter. Which selection is most defensible?
choices: Select whichever process already has a discounted software proposal
Split the funding equally before assessing either process in detail
Pilot equipment requests with measurable benefits and bounded risk
Select medication authorization because its potential consequences are greater
rationale: The equipment process offers an understood, bounded opportunity consistent with the stated short-term objective. Safety-critical authorization deserves analysis but carries greater uncertainty for this first project. Splitting scarce funding can prevent a meaningful outcome, while a software discount does not establish business priority or process suitability.

stem: Order fulfillment must coordinate credit checks, inventory reservation, carrier booking, and staff exceptions across three enterprise applications and an external logistics company. Which solution class best fits the need for coordinated execution and monitoring across those boundaries?
choices: A shared repository with document versioning and general update subscriptions
Separate departmental approval workflows joined by untracked email notifications
A BPM platform supporting system integrations and human activities
RPA scripts that copy completed transactions overnight without end-to-end state coordination
rationale: The requirement includes coordinated execution across systems and an external organization, which calls for integrated process management. Departmental flows with untracked email leave cross-boundary state unclear. Overnight copying does not coordinate reservation and booking or human exceptions. Versioning and subscriptions support content collaboration but do not provide the required orchestration.

stem: A communications team manages thousands of licensed photographs and videos. Staff need thumbnails, format renditions, and searches using media-specific properties. A proposed document repository mainly supports office files. Which capability deserves priority in evaluation?
choices: A synchronization service that distributes unchanged originals to local editing tools
Digital asset management supporting media properties, renditions, and licensing workflows
An imaging platform that creates previews while flattening media-specific properties
A document repository with large-file support but only office-document metadata
rationale: Digital asset management should be evaluated because the required functions concern rich-media management. Large-file storage establishes capacity, synchronization supports distribution, and imaging previews support viewing. None of those narrower demonstrations establishes the licensing context, renditions, and media-specific retrieval the team needs to manage its collection effectively.

stem: Sales will move to a new repository before operations. Both teams update active cases, and a tested cross-system handoff can transfer ownership at a chosen milestone. The project must avoid conflicting current versions during the mixed period. Which transition design most directly controls that risk?
choices: Use a single naming convention and rely on the newest modification timestamp to select authority
Copy active cases nightly and let each department correct discrepancies during its weekly review
Give both teams read access everywhere while allowing each to update its own repository copy
Define ownership by case milestone and enforce the tested transfer between systems
rationale: An explicit ownership boundary and controlled transfer establish which system may hold the current record at each stage. Nightly copying permits conflicts between reconciliations. Broad read access does not govern competing writes. Names and timestamps help identify objects but cannot determine business authority when updates occur independently.

stem: An agency must release two differently redacted versions of the same investigation report to different authorized recipients. The redaction tool removes content properly. Which additional control most directly makes the differing disclosures explainable later?
choices: Retain the master and a reusable redaction template without preserving recipient-specific output
Retain each released rendition with its redaction decisions and recipient context
Keep each rendition but discard the reasons once recipients acknowledge delivery
Preserve approval emails and page counts without retaining the exact disclosed renditions
rationale: The actual released versions and reasons for differences establish what each recipient received and why. A master and template may not reproduce the executed release. Renditions without reasons cannot explain challenged redactions. Approval emails and page counts do not establish the exact content disclosed to each recipient.

stem: A newly acquired subsidiary operates in a different country and industry from its parent. Before applying the parent information governance policies, which fact set is most useful for identifying where local requirements may differ?
choices: Operating model, jurisdictions, industry obligations, and business processes
Staff headcount, office floor area, and equipment age
Storage consumption, software release dates, and network bandwidth
Folder depth, file extensions, and average document size
rationale: Operating model, jurisdictions, industry context, and work processes establish the governance environment and the obligations that must be examined. Storage and software facts support technical planning; staffing and facilities support resource planning; file characteristics support inventory work. Those alternatives cannot establish the subsidiary business and regulatory context.

stem: A product company proposes combining governed customer feedback with design knowledge to identify unmet needs and shorten product development. Which strategic benefit of intelligent information management is most directly represented by the proposal?
choices: Achieving compliance solely by centralizing all customer information
Replacing product management judgment with a repository implementation
Reducing storage expenditure by deleting every feedback record sooner
Enabling innovation through better use of existing information assets
rationale: The proposal uses information to create improved products and shorten development, directly supporting innovation. No disposal or storage-saving mechanism is described. Information can inform judgment without replacing product management. Centralization alone does not establish compliance, and compliance is not the specific benefit emphasized by this proposal.

stem: An LLM drafts an emergency procedure from approved manuals. It adds plausible steps supported by citations reviewers cannot locate. Release is urgent, and the draft includes valid material. Which review decision best balances usefulness with reliability?
choices: Verify consequential claims against approved sources, revise unsupported steps, and obtain accountable expert approval
Remove only the unlocatable citations while preserving their associated instructions as general professional advice
Ask a second LLM to confirm the missing citations and release if both answers agree
Validate a sample of accurate passages and release the remaining steps with an AI-assistance disclosure
rationale: The draft can be useful, but consequential instructions need source-backed expert validation before release. Sampling valid passages does not validate unsupported steps; agreement between models is not authoritative evidence; removing citations leaves the underlying claims unverified. Disclosure is appropriate context but does not substitute for evaluating operational correctness.

stem: A support director wants to discover recurring concerns in thousands of free-text service notes before choosing improvement projects. Counting customer names is already possible. Which analytics use case most directly addresses the new need?
choices: Extract customer and agent identities into a directory of mentioned people
Identify and group recurring topics across the service notes
Select one representative sentence from each note without grouping related issues
Assign positive or negative sentiment without identifying the underlying concern
rationale: Recurring topic recognition directly supports discovery of concerns across the collection. Entity extraction identifies who appears, sentiment measures tone without necessarily explaining the issue, and individual summaries condense documents without grouping shared concerns. Each can complement analysis, but the requested improvement planning first needs thematic evidence.

stem: A migration budget covers only sixty percent of a repository. Recent-access filtering would include many convenience copies but exclude older records under continuing obligations. Some active reports depend on older reference files. Which scope decision is most defensible?
choices: Select the oldest required records first and use the remaining budget for arbitrary active files
Migrate all active documents and defer their older dependencies to a later project
Migrate the most recently accessed sixty percent and retain a catalogue of the excluded remainder
Prioritize required records and dependencies, then assess valuable active content and documented exclusions
rationale: Scope must account for obligations, dependencies, and business value rather than a single age or usage metric. A catalogue cannot replace excluded required content; active documents can be unusable without reference dependencies; and arbitrary allocation after selecting old records lacks a justified assessment of remaining business needs and exclusion risks.

stem: An employee mistakenly publishes a spreadsheet containing client bank details. The incident is confirmed, and the file remains publicly downloadable. Which coordinated response is most appropriate while the team assesses exposure and notification obligations?
choices: Delete the exposed copy and its logs to eliminate any remaining personal information
Remove public access promptly while preserving evidence and assessing affected information
Notify every client immediately using an unverified estimate of affected accounts
Finish tracing every download before changing the publicly accessible link
rationale: Containment should stop the known ongoing exposure while evidence supports assessment and legally coordinated notification. Exhaustive download tracing should not prolong public access. Premature notices with unverified scope can mislead recipients. Deleting logs removes information needed to determine impact and defend the response rather than simply reducing exposure.

stem: Counsel confirms a three-year minimum for equipment inspection records and no legal maximum. Engineering demonstrates that six years of inspection history is needed to diagnose failures across the service cycle. What should the schedule reflect?
choices: Separate unofficial engineering copies beyond the three-year scheduled period
Indefinite retention because engineering has identified some continuing value
A three-year period because statutory minima prohibit longer business retention
A documented six-year requirement approved through the governance process
rationale: A justified operational requirement may extend retention beyond a statutory minimum when no competing maximum applies. It should be documented and agreed with relevant functions. A minimum does not forbid longer retention. Indefinite retention exceeds the demonstrated six-year need, and unofficial copies bypass consistent lifecycle management.

stem: An extraction model meets pilot targets. Production will triple volume and introduce new form families. Funding covers cloud capacity and vendor technical support, but nobody owns exception decisions or business-rule maintenance. Which rollout condition best addresses the unresolved risk?
choices: Expand after purchasing additional cloud capacity and rely on vendor incident support for operational decisions
Assign and resource business monitoring, exception authority, and model-maintenance responsibilities before expanding scope
Expand at the pilot confidence threshold and have users report errors when they notice them
Raise the confidence threshold and classify the resulting manual queue as outside the project's scope
rationale: Production introduces both workload and model-management needs. Technical capacity and incident support do not assign authority for business exceptions or evolving rules. Passive reporting may miss systematic problems, and a higher threshold can enlarge an unowned queue. Accountable operating responsibilities are necessary to make the proposed expansion supportable.

stem: An expense workflow already records approval, payment, employee identity, and transaction date. Staff then retype those facts into a records screen, producing omissions. Which automation offers the strongest direct improvement?
choices: Copy workflow metadata automatically but require staff to declare completion independently in each system
Capture the completed expense record using validated workflow data and status
Retain monthly screenshots of the workflow instead of capturing the completed transaction records
Capture the initial claim immediately and discard later approval metadata as administrative detail
rationale: Validated workflow data and the completion state can produce consistent records with less rekeying. Capturing only the initial claim omits later evidence. Independent duplicate declarations preserve the inconsistency the project seeks to remove. Monthly screenshots are a weaker substitute for complete transaction records with associated structured context.

stem: A policy review requires subject experts to comment, an editor to revise, and a designated official to approve publication. Which combination of collaboration features most directly supports these distinct responsibilities?
choices: Separate expert review copies, editor reconciliation, and approval identified only in filenames
Role-based access, version comparison, and approval of the controlled document
A common document with comments but no distinct publication-approval role
A shared editable draft, email signoff, and a folder containing the editor's latest copy
rationale: The first design implements different participation rights and ties approval to a managed version. Email signoffs and separate review copies can work only with further controls not demonstrated here, while filenames are weak approval evidence. A shared comments-only arrangement does not establish who can authorize the controlled document's publication.

stem: A service team manually rekeys the same routing fields from thousands of standardized forms. Individual operators use different abbreviations, causing correction queues. Which expected benefit should lead the extraction business case?
choices: Faster raw extraction measured without including required correction effort
Broader field completion using existing inconsistent abbreviations unchanged
Reduced headcount calculated before determining which exceptions still need review
Consistent field population that reduces rekeying and downstream correction work
rationale: The expected benefit should address the actual cause of rework: inconsistent repeated entry. Raw extraction speed excludes downstream costs, premature staffing reductions ignore exception work, and completing more fields with inconsistent meanings preserves the defect. Agreed fields and evaluated automation can improve consistency, accuracy, and usable processing efficiency together.

stem: New employees cannot describe unfamiliar product issues using the specialist terms in the knowledge base. Experienced staff find exact terms quickly. Which findability design best serves both populations?
choices: Replace full-text retrieval with one comprehensive hierarchy covering every exception
Expand all queries to every related specialist term without offering contextual filters
Combine meaningful category navigation with search and consistent metadata
Require exact-phrase queries supported by a downloadable glossary of specialist terms
rationale: Category navigation helps users lacking exact terms, while metadata and search retain targeted retrieval for experienced staff. A glossary can help but still requires term selection, an exhaustive hierarchy may be burdensome and removes useful text search, and unfiltered expansion can increase noise without supporting purposeful navigation.

stem: Two clerical tasks take the same total staff hours. One uses stable screens and fixed validation rules; the other handles many customer-specific layouts and requires interpretation. The proposed bots have similar license costs. Which factor most favors automating the first task?
choices: Lower support costs inferred solely from the similar bot license prices
Greater return inferred from running the bot without defining exception ownership
Lower exception-handling and maintenance effort for repeatable interactions
A larger labor-release benefit simply because fewer input formats are involved
rationale: Stable structures and fixed rules reduce configuration, maintenance, and exception effort, strengthening the first task’s economics. Equal total labor hours do not imply a larger gross release for it. Similar license prices do not establish similar support costs. Omitting exception ownership can hide costs and failure risks rather than improve return.

stem: A research archive must reproduce a legacy simulation's interactive behavior for ten years. Conversion preserves input data but changes some outputs. Tested emulation reproduces required behavior; original hardware is failing. Which preservation plan best meets the stated acceptance criterion?
choices: Preserve native objects with tested emulation, documented dependencies, and periodic behavior checks
Convert the simulation and document output differences as acceptable preservation losses
Keep original hardware operational and postpone emulation until the last machine fails
Migrate the inputs and retain published outputs as the complete preserved representation
rationale: The acceptance criterion is reproducible interactive behavior, which the tested emulator currently satisfies. Inputs and published outputs do not reproduce interaction; delaying a viable method preserves a fragile hardware dependency. Documenting conversion losses is useful evidence, but cannot make losses acceptable when they defeat the specified preservation requirement.

stem: An approved three-year IM roadmap includes several projects. A merger changes priorities and available funding after year one. Which use of the roadmap best preserves its value as a guide for the program?
choices: Discard completed work and restart every assessment from the beginning
Replace the roadmap with the next vendor’s recommended product sequence
Reassess remaining work against new goals, dependencies and resources
Treat the original project dates as fixed regardless of changed circumstances
rationale: A roadmap provides a path forward as circumstances, priorities, and resources change. Reviewing remaining projects preserves useful completed work while realigning future actions. Fixed dates can become disconnected from business needs. Restarting everything wastes valid work, and a vendor sequence cannot substitute for the organization’s priorities.

stem: IT has built a procurement repository but cannot determine whether contract negotiators need read access or editing rights to signed agreements. Which approach best establishes appropriate permissions before rollout?
choices: Use repository access logs alone to infer the permissions each job requires
Have process owners define permitted activities and translate them into roles
Copy the unsigned-draft role because both stages are handled by the contracts department
Give every negotiator the permissions held by the most experienced current negotiator
rationale: Process owners should define the activities each role may perform, including the distinction between negotiation and executed agreements. Copying an experienced user may reproduce accumulated excessive access. Usage logs do not establish legitimate unused needs or prohibited activities. An unsigned-draft role may wrongly permit alteration of signed evidence.

stem: A company has hundreds of project spaces. After projects finish, membership lists remain active and nobody answers questions about their documents. What governance measure most directly closes this responsibility gap?
choices: Require project closure reports but retain all workspace memberships until content disposal
Make IT responsible for storage while leaving content and membership decisions informal
Assign accountable space owners and define closure and membership-review duties
Disable all inactive spaces automatically after a fixed period without owner review
rationale: Ownership and specific lifecycle duties address the observed accountability gap. Automatic inactivity closure may interrupt justified access or obligations, storage administration alone leaves business decisions unowned, and a closure report does not justify continued membership. Workspace content and access require active responsibility beyond initial project completion.

stem: A program aims to increase managers' confidence in the information used for decisions. Direct financial attribution is impractical. Which measurement approach best respects the nature of this benefit while still permitting meaningful progress review?
choices: Repeat a consistent confidence survey and examine supporting quality evidence
Convert every favorable survey response into an arbitrary dollar saving
Use total license expenditure as a proxy for confidence gained
Exclude the benefit because it lacks a direct monetary measure
rationale: Intangible benefits can be assessed through consistent surveys or indirect measures, with supporting evidence strengthening interpretation. An arbitrary monetary conversion invents precision. Excluding the benefit ignores a relevant objective, while expenditure measures investment rather than the confidence or information quality that the program seeks to improve.

stem: A governance lead inherits extensive policies but finds three divisions using unofficial spreadsheets to approve access. Before proposing a replacement platform, what assessment best explains the gap between documented governance and actual practice?
choices: Ask division managers to certify that the published policy adequately describes their practice
Consolidate all approval spreadsheets into the existing repository before evaluating decision rights
Audit spreadsheet access permissions and treat compliant permissions as sufficient governance
Compare formal rules with real workflows, responsibilities, tools, and constraints
rationale: Evaluation should compare actual and formal practices, including responsibilities, resources, and constraints. Consolidating spreadsheets may improve storage but can preserve a defective approval process. Permission auditing addresses only access. Management certification is useful evidence, but without examining the actual workflows it may reproduce the gap rather than explain it.

stem: A digitally signed report must be shared with analysts. The original signature verifies, but an analyst proposes modifying the signed report to add commentary while retaining the visible signature mark. Which design best preserves both attributable source evidence and the ability to develop analysis?
choices: Retain the signed report intact and manage commentary as clearly related separate content
Have the analyst digitally sign the revised report and replace the source with that version
Record the original verification result once and retain only the commented report thereafter
Allow commentary within the report provided the visible signature mark remains on every page
rationale: Keeping the signed source intact preserves evidence attributable to its signer, while related commentary can develop independently. A visible mark does not preserve cryptographic coverage after modification. The analyst can sign a new work but cannot replace the original signer’s evidence. A historical verification entry does not make the modified report the signed original.

stem: Applicants must provide an internal billing code that only employees know. Staff call each applicant, then supply the code themselves. Finance confirms it is derivable from the selected service and has no separate customer attestation purpose. What redesign best addresses the cause?
choices: Add more staff to make applicant clarification calls
Derive the code from the service selection within intake
Reject submissions until applicants learn the internal billing codes
Move the same clarification call to the final review stage
rationale: The input asks customers for information the organization already knows how to derive, causing avoidable rework. Deriving it during intake removes the defect at its source. More callers increase capacity without removing the cause. Rejection transfers internal complexity to customers, while moving the call merely shifts the delay downstream.

stem: Legal counsel confirms that a particular national dataset must remain locally stored and accessible only to locally authorized staff. The global platform supports regional storage but a worldwide support team can read every region. What design change is necessary?
choices: Mask direct names for support staff while leaving other identifying records fully accessible
Allow worldwide support through logged sessions because the content remains locally stored
Select local storage and rely on confidentiality clauses for the worldwide support team
Restrict support access as well as selecting the permitted storage region
rationale: The confirmed rule restricts both storage and access to locally authorized staff. Contractual confidentiality and logged access do not make worldwide staff locally authorized. Masking names may reduce exposure, but the scenario does not establish that all identifying information is removed or that this satisfies the specific access restriction.

stem: A purchasing workflow routes items to Elena by name. She transfers departments next month, and two qualified employees will share her former responsibility. What design change most directly makes assignment resilient to future personnel changes?
choices: Create separate permanent copies addressed to both replacement employees
Route all requests to the executive sponsor for reassignment
Keep Elena assigned and ask her to forward each request
Route to the defined purchasing role with maintained membership
rationale: Role-based routing attaches work to a defined function and permits authorized people in that role to take it when staffing changes. Duplicate copies create competing ownership. Manual forwarding preserves dependence on Elena, while executive reassignment creates unnecessary handling and a new concentration of routine work.

stem: Users agree to written requirements but cannot picture how a new classification screen will affect their work. They give conflicting explanations of a typical submission. Which elicitation technique best makes these differences concrete before detailed development?
choices: Circulate another survey repeating the same terms used in the written requirements
Walk representative users through a prototype using realistic submission examples
Ask an expert to finalize the screen based on the conflicting descriptions
Approve the requirements now and explain the intended interpretation during rollout training
rationale: A realistic prototype makes the proposed interaction concrete and exposes how users interpret it. Another survey using the same ambiguous language may reproduce the disagreement. Expert design without user validation can embed assumptions. Deferring clarification to training discovers requirement conflicts after the system has already been committed and built.

stem: Different branch offices retain the same class of settled expense claims for different periods because clerks decide individually. Which instrument primarily establishes consistent lifecycle treatment for this class across the organization?
choices: A backup calendar applied to each branch storage server
An approved retention schedule applied to the records series
A file naming convention applied to each reimbursement document
A staff directory identifying each branch finance supervisor
rationale: A retention schedule groups records with shared characteristics and assigns consistent retention and disposition requirements. Naming helps identification but does not authorize retention periods. Backup calendars address recovery copies rather than the lifecycle of the records series. A directory identifies people without specifying how long claims should be retained.

stem: An IM strategy identifies 'reliable access to approved operating instructions' as a critical success factor. Which proposed KPI most directly measures progress toward that factor, using a defined sample of employees' genuine work tasks?
choices: Percentage of tasks retrieving the current approved instruction within target time
Total number of documents imported during the initial migration weekend
Number of communications announcing the new information strategy to employees
Percentage of the project budget committed to repository licenses
rationale: The proposed retrieval measure tests both correctness and timeliness of access to approved instructions. Announcements, imported document counts, and license expenditure describe activities or inputs. Those may support the program, but they do not directly establish that employees can retrieve the right instruction when needed.

stem: A document legitimately supports three programs. Its source metadata holds three program values, but the receiving application permits one. The integration team proposes copying only the first value. Which design best preserves cross-system findability?
choices: Represent all valid program relationships in the target and test retrieval through each one
Concatenate all values into one opaque identifier and use exact-match searching
Duplicate the document into three unrelated objects without preserving their common identity
Select the program used most often and record the other values only in a migration log
rationale: Metadata interoperability must preserve the source concept's multiplicity, not just move a field. Keeping one value loses valid discovery paths, an opaque combined identifier changes query meaning, and unrelated duplicate objects fragment identity. A supported representation of the relationships should be validated through the actual retrieval tasks.

stem: A media company needs frame-level video editing and controlled contract approval. Existing specialized repositories meet those needs, while a proposed single platform lacks frame-level editing. Staff need cross-department discovery, and all choices must retain mandatory capabilities. Which first architecture option should be evaluated most seriously?
choices: Create a central duplicate collection updated quarterly from the specialized repositories
Keep both repositories unchanged and provide users a directory of system links
Federate discovery with common governance while retaining the specialized repositories
Migrate both collections to the single platform and retain exports for occasional editing
rationale: Federation can preserve mandatory specialized functions while addressing cross-department discovery, subject to governance and integration validation. Exports do not demonstrate equivalent ongoing editing capability. A link directory does not supply unified discovery. Quarterly duplication creates stale competing copies and additional controls without establishing that the central view meets work needs.

stem: A maintenance department receives equipment warnings from sensors, telephone reports from operators, and messages from contractors. Its intake inventory lists only documents uploaded to the maintenance portal. What should the information professional add first?
choices: All channels through which actionable maintenance information enters
All departments with access to the maintenance repository
All reports created after maintenance jobs are closed
All file extensions accepted by the maintenance portal
rationale: Entry-point analysis follows information into the process, including machine signals and spoken reports that can trigger work. File extensions describe one channel, access lists identify users rather than origins, and closing reports are downstream outputs rather than the missing intake routes.

stem: A museum corporate archive has accepted a company founding charter for permanent preservation after its active business use ends. The approved schedule calls for transfer. Which action implements that disposition instruction?
choices: Retain a reference copy in a departmental folder and mark transfer complete
Export the charter and context to the designated archive
Delete the source record at expiry without confirming archival receipt
Transfer only a thumbnail image and discard the contextual record metadata
rationale: Authorized archival transfer should deliver the record and its necessary context to the designated archive. Expiry does not authorize deletion before the transfer is completed. A departmental reference copy is not the specified archive, and a thumbnail without context does not preserve the charter as a usable archival record.

stem: A supplier offers portal approvals recorded under named user accounts, followed by a cryptographic seal issued to the supplier company. The buyer needs evidence of which individual approved the exact final content. Which acceptance test most directly determines whether the combined process meets that need?
choices: Compare the displayed approver name with the company directory and retain the final file
Verify that the named user logged in on the approval date and retain the daily login report
Verify the company seal on the final file and accept the company identity as individual attribution
Trace the authenticated individual approval to the exact sealed version and preserve that evidence
rationale: The combined process must connect an authenticated individual action with the precise content approved. A valid company seal can protect that content without identifying the individual approver. A daily login establishes access rather than approval of a version. A displayed directory name is likewise weaker than evidence of the actual authenticated action.

stem: Business users request an approval-screen redesign, while IT believes the underlying problem involves routing rules. The implementation team needs the needs clarified and translated into agreed requirements before configuration. Which role should lead that work?
choices: An executive sponsor authorizing investment using the agreed program business case
A business analyst eliciting and reconciling needs with users and the solution team
A system administrator applying configuration settings from the finalized requirements baseline
A procurement lead comparing supplier quotations against an already approved specification
rationale: The analyst bridges business and solution perspectives by eliciting needs, resolving interpretations, and recommending requirements that address the problem. Procurement compares commercial offers, the sponsor authorizes or supports investment, and administration implements approved settings. Those roles are important but do not replace the required clarification before a baseline exists.

stem: A utility has twelve years of paper inspection files. Active facilities account for most retrievals; older closed-facility files receive few requests. New inspections will become digital immediately, and funding cannot cover the entire archive. Which strategy best fits?
choices: Digitize the oldest files first and delay new digital capture
Digitize every file before allowing the new inspection process
Digitize active-facility backfiles and capture new inspections digitally
Scan historical files only when requested and postpone active-file conversion
rationale: A selective backfile conversion concentrates resources on frequently needed material while day-forward capture prevents further paper accumulation. Oldest-first sequencing ignores use, full conversion exceeds the constraint, and request-only conversion would leave the repeatedly used active collection unnecessarily dependent on paper.

stem: A supplier response is due Friday, followed by two business days of internal review before a Monday customer deadline. Management wants intervention before the customer commitment is missed. Which report is most useful today?
choices: A report ranking completed requests by their historical average cycle time
A reviewer utilization report aggregated across the current calendar month
A report showing supplier due dates without internal review dependencies
Dependency-aware jeopardy reporting identifying the threatened downstream deadline
rationale: Jeopardy reporting connects the supplier dependency with the remaining review time and customer commitment, enabling timely intervention. Supplier dates alone can appear acceptable while the downstream deadline is impossible. Historical averages and monthly utilization may support improvement, but they do not identify the specific active commitment threatened by this sequence.

stem: A claims application already protects finalized case records, applies retention rules, supports holds, and logs actions. Moving every record would break links used by claims staff. What is the strongest reason to manage those records in place?
choices: Keep only a central search index and withdraw the application's existing lifecycle controls
Preserve business context and workflow while applying records controls in the application
Create a second authoritative copy so two systems can independently make retention decisions
Export final records immediately even though doing so severs required operational relationships
rationale: The application already meets required controls, so managing in place preserves useful relationships without unnecessary movement. Independently authoritative duplicates can create conflicting lifecycle decisions. Immediate export loses stipulated context. A search index improves discovery but does not replace the controls required for the records retained in the application.

stem: An authorized editor accidentally publishes a procedure with an incorrect safety limit. The previous approved version remains in the repository. Which document-management capability most directly restores the usable publication while retaining its history?
choices: Create a second repository containing a manually corrected procedure
Remove the current file and reimport the previous version separately
Change the document identifier to prevent access to its history
Revert publication to the previous approved version with an audit entry
rationale: Rollback restores a prior usable version while preserving the sequence of events. A second repository creates competing locations, changing identifiers obscures continuity, and deleting and reimporting can detach the historical record. The correction should remain attributable rather than erase evidence of publication.

stem: An insurer knows which applications it owns but cannot explain how claim photographs move from field inspectors to outsourced assessors. It needs to identify handoffs and exposure points. Which inventory should provide the main organizing framework?
choices: An equipment inventory recording device locations and replacement dates
A process inventory tracing information inputs, handoffs, and outputs
A systems inventory listing product versions and support dates
A media inventory counting image formats and storage capacities
rationale: A process inventory follows information through activities and organizational boundaries, exposing the handoffs in question. A systems inventory identifies applications but does not explain the flow. Equipment location and media capacity may contribute facts, but neither supplies the process relationships needed to understand how the photographs reach assessors.

stem: A distributor finds that sales and finance use different meanings of active customer. A database administrator can change fields but cannot decide which business definition should apply. Who should lead resolution of the meaning?
choices: Database administrators working through the infrastructure change board
Software developers working through the application release process
Business stewards working with the affected business functions
External auditors working through the annual assurance program
rationale: Stewards are accountable for business meaning, quality, and usefulness across functions. Business agreement must guide the technical change. Database administrators can implement the definition, auditors can assess compliance with it, and developers can encode it, but none of those technical or assurance roles independently determines the business meaning.

stem: Using the same sampling method, a process finds that incomplete outputs fell from eight percent to two percent after automated completeness checks. Volume and case mix stayed constant. Which benefit claim is best supported before any wider financial or customer research is performed?
choices: A guaranteed improvement in customer satisfaction proportional to the change
A six-percent reduction in every category of process cost
An eight-percent reduction in the volume of cases requiring service
A six-percentage-point reduction in the observed incomplete-output rate
rationale: The measured rate decreased by six percentage points, or seventy-five percent relative to its previous level. That directly supports an output-quality benefit under the stated comparison conditions. It does not establish a matching cost reduction, lower service demand, or a quantified customer-satisfaction effect without further evidence.

stem: A purchasing analyst needs to find a purchase order and immediately approve it within the purchasing application. Relevant data is confined to that application. Which search approach most directly supports this task?
choices: Deploy a cross-enterprise index before searching purchase orders
Export purchase orders to a separate general document library
Use the application's search and its native transaction actions
Search a daily PDF report and reenter the identified order
rationale: Application search operates where the user is working and can make results directly actionable within its security and data model. An enterprise index adds unnecessary scope, exporting creates another location, and a PDF report introduces an extra handoff and may lag the application's current transaction state.

stem: A company agrees its metadata field names and permitted values, but departments keep changing definitions independently. Which additional element most directly makes the metadata strategy maintainable across systems over time?
choices: Named stewards with responsibility for definitions and controlled changes
A published comparison of each repository's storage capacity
A longer list of optional fields for future business needs
A requirement to display all fields on every upload form
rationale: Stewardship assigns accountability for definitions and their maintenance, helping preserve consistency after the initial design. Additional optional fields expand the model without governing it. Capacity information does not govern semantics, and exposing every field changes the interface rather than controlling who can revise shared definitions.

stem: A community of practice identifies inconsistent customer classifications. The center of excellence proposes a standard, but two executives reject the associated business changes. Who should resolve the enterprise priority and accountability conflict?
choices: The community of practice, choosing a standard by practitioner consensus without delegated authority
The center of excellence, imposing its recommended standard as a technical change
The two executives independently, allowing incompatible definitions to remain enterprise defaults
The steering committee, escalating beyond its mandate to the program owner
rationale: The steering committee resolves strategic and cross-functional conflicts within its mandate, escalating when necessary. The center of excellence supplies expertise but cannot assume executive authority. Separate incompatible defaults leave the enterprise issue unresolved. Practitioner consensus is useful input but cannot substitute for a decision by accountable authorized leadership.

stem: A purchased industry taxonomy matches most of a firm's work, but omits one important service and includes several irrelevant branches. The firm values partner interoperability and has limited development time. Which approach fits best?
choices: Build an entirely new scheme using only the firm's internal terminology
Use independent departmental schemes and reconcile results after deployment
Implement every purchased branch and classify the new service as miscellaneous
Modify the purchased scheme while documenting local extensions and removals
rationale: Adapting the existing scheme retains much of its interoperability and speed while addressing genuine local needs. A full rebuild consumes time and may lose alignment; unmodified adoption leaves a core service poorly represented; independent schemes defer rather than resolve the cross-organizational consistency requirement.

stem: A process diagram shows a completeness check with a path to assessment when evidence is complete. The incomplete branch ends without an activity or terminator, although staff normally request evidence and resume review. Which correction is most necessary?
choices: Show the request and return path to a defined decision point
Remove incomplete applications from the documented process boundary
Rename the completeness check without changing its connecting paths
Replace the decision symbol with the same generic task rectangle
rationale: Every decision path should resolve to another activity or a defined end. Showing the evidence request and return makes the actual sequence understandable. A renamed check leaves the missing behavior unresolved. A task rectangle conceals the branch, and excluding incomplete submissions omits a known part of the process.

stem: Two proposed service designs have the same number of boxes and decision points. One requires a specialist shared with another department, and demand fluctuates sharply. What additional analysis is needed before claiming that the designs have equal completion times?
choices: Compare average labor cost per task using the current staffing budget
Sum average task durations assuming the specialist is dedicated to each design
Model resource availability, task durations, demand, and external dependencies
Simulate both designs with uniform arrivals and permanently available specialist capacity
rationale: A flowchart’s shape does not establish timing under variable demand and shared resources. Modeling the actual availability and dependencies tests the key difference. Summed durations omit contention, and labor cost does not establish elapsed time. A simulation with uniform arrivals and dedicated capacity would conceal the very constraints described.

stem: For a three-year evaluation, Solution A costs $60,000 initially plus $24,000 annually; Solution B costs $18,000 initially plus $39,000 annually. All other costs are equal; ignore discounting and taxes. What does the stated cost comparison show?
choices: B costs $42,000 less over the three-year period
B costs $3,000 less over the three-year period
A costs $3,000 less over the three-year period
A costs $15,000 less over the three-year period
rationale: A totals $60,000 plus three times $24,000, or $132,000. B totals $18,000 plus three times $39,000, or $135,000. Thus A is $3,000 lower. The $42,000 figure compares only initial costs; $15,000 compares annual costs. Reversing the $3,000 result misidentifies the less expensive option.

stem: A membership team says it has no process because there is no procedure manual. Staff nevertheless receive applications, check payment, request missing evidence, and issue decisions. What conclusion should an analyst draw from this initial observation?
choices: A process exists only for applications receiving favorable decisions
Automation must wait until the department creates formal job titles
A process exists and its actual rules require investigation
The activities are unrelated because they lack approved documentation
rationale: Recurring linked activities can constitute a process even when undocumented. The analyst should investigate triggers, outcomes, rules, and exceptions before assessing automation. Formal job titles do not establish whether a process exists. Lack of documentation does not make related work unrelated, and unfavorable decisions remain legitimate process outcomes.

stem: A distributor’s order process remains profitable, but new competitors let customers change delivery instructions after ordering. Research shows customers increasingly expect this capability. Which reason most directly supports redesign before current revenue begins to decline?
choices: Reducing transaction errors already demonstrated in existing operations
Maintaining market relevance as customer expectations change
Resolving a currently binding statutory processing requirement
Recovering acquisition costs already spent on existing software
rationale: The evidence concerns a changing market and future relevance, so redesign can protect the organization’s competitive position before revenue falls. No error trend or statutory requirement is given. Prior acquisition spending is a sunk cost; recovering it does not explain why the process now needs to change.

stem: A team has tested export tools and wants to begin bulk migration tomorrow. The target repository has no final classification, metadata, or access-control structures. What should happen before the transfer begins?
choices: Transfer the content first and assign controls after users discover it
Freeze the source and let the migration utility choose target defaults
Complete and validate the target structures required for managed ingestion
Copy files into temporary user folders while designing the repository
rationale: Target design is part of migration preparation, enabling information to arrive with the required structure and controls. Postponing controls creates avoidable exposure and rework, utility defaults cannot decide business requirements, and temporary user folders introduce another unmanaged transfer without resolving the missing target design.

stem: A stakeholder states, 'Our field inspectors need to consult approved procedures while working.' The architect immediately specifies a particular database brand. What should the requirements team do to preserve the distinction between business need and technical constraints?
choices: Replace the business statement with the preferred database product specification
Reject the business statement because it contains no implementation technology
Document the access need, then derive justified system and environmental requirements
Treat the database brand as a proven user requirement without validation
rationale: Business requirements express the capability with value to users; system and domain requirements translate that need into specific constraints and behavior. A preferred database may be justified later, but substituting it prematurely obscures the need. Lack of a named technology is appropriate at the business level, not a reason to reject it.

stem: A maintenance team saves inspection results but omits the asset identifier and the inspector identity. Months later, it cannot connect a result to a particular machine. Which recordkeeping purpose was most directly missed?
choices: Consolidating unrelated records into a common electronic format
Reducing the storage cost of completed inspection documents
Increasing the number of users who can edit results
Linking the evidence to its creator and business context
rationale: Capturing a record establishes its relationship to the creator and the business event or asset. Without that context the result has limited evidentiary usefulness. Lower storage cost and common formats may help operations but do not repair the missing relationship. More editors would not identify the inspection and could weaken control.

stem: A former contractor controls a project message account and offers to send selected screenshots in response to a dispute. Counsel needs reliable evidence of the full relevant conversation. What should the information professional recommend?
choices: Coordinate lawful collection with counsel, preserving context and provenance
Ask another employee to access the account using a saved password
Retype the messages into a spreadsheet to standardize the collection
Accept the selected screenshots as a complete substitute for source messages
rationale: Third-party collection presents both access and authentication challenges. Counsel should direct a lawful method that preserves relevant context and provenance. Selected screenshots may omit material and weaken authentication. Using someone else’s saved password is not an established collection authority, and retyping strips the source metadata without establishing completeness.

stem: A company replaces emailed service requests with a supplier portal. Internal staff already know the tool, but small suppliers have limited technical support. Which implementation impact should the team explicitly include when assessing the change?
choices: Supplier submission practices, access support, and transition communications
Only supplier contract pricing because submission behavior is unchanged
Only the company’s employees because suppliers are outside program scope
Only server capacity because internal staff already understand the tool
rationale: Changing the submission channel affects suppliers' work and access needs even when internal users are comfortable. External stakeholders can be materially affected by an IM initiative. Excluding them misses adoption barriers. Server capacity is only one concern, and the new channel changes submission behavior independently of contract pricing.

stem: A permit identifier must contain two letters followed by six digits. Operators often transpose letters and numbers, although the correct pattern is documented. Which entry control most directly rejects structurally invalid identifiers?
choices: Offer a longer free-text field with additional explanatory notes
Make the identifier optional until the permit is approved
Populate the field with the last identifier entered by that operator
Apply a field mask enforcing the required character pattern
rationale: A mask validates the required character structure at entry. More space and instructions still permit malformed input; reusing a prior value risks assigning the wrong identifier; optional entry postpones completeness. Pattern validation improves structural quality but does not alone prove the identifier belongs to the correct permit.

stem: A researcher receives employee shift records without names. Each row contains a rare job title, exact work location, and shift time, and the public staff directory can identify the individual. How should the organization initially classify these rows?
choices: As organizational data because the activities occurred at work
As public data because a separate directory is public
As personal data because individuals can be identified indirectly
As anonymous data because names were excluded during export
rationale: Personal data includes information that identifies someone indirectly through combinations of attributes. Removing names does not establish anonymity when other reasonably available information identifies people. Work activity can still concern an identifiable person, and a public directory does not make the separate shift records unrestricted or remove their personal character.

stem: A company already groups documents by stable business activity. It wants to apply different retention and access rules consistently without asking authors to choose every rule separately. Which extension best uses the taxonomy?
choices: Associate validated governance rules with classes and manage their application
Add lifecycle descriptions to category labels without configuring or governing their application
Map every class to the strictest existing rule and reassess only after complaints
Ask authors to choose independent retention and access values alongside each class
rationale: Class-linked rules use established business context to support consistent governance. Independent repeated selections add burden and opportunities for contradiction, maximum controls may be inappropriate for some classes, and descriptive labels do not by themselves implement rules. Mappings and their application need validation, accountability, and maintenance.

stem: A manufacturer wants to track supplier disputes involving contracts, inspection findings, correspondence, negotiations, and agreed remedies. Each dispute follows different investigative steps within a common opening and closure policy. Which approach most directly matches this work?
choices: A fixed contract-approval route applied separately to each dispute document
An RPA queue that transfers correspondence between the existing systems
A supplier relationship record with contact alerts but no separate dispute lifecycle
Case management for the dispute and its related content
rationale: The dispute needs coordinated evidence and variable investigative activity toward a bounded resolution. Separate document approval routes fragment that work. RPA can assist transfers without choosing the investigative path. A supplier-level record may support several disputes but cannot replace their individual evidence, actions, and resolution responsibilities.

stem: An archive must accept a collection in six weeks. Storage and integrity checking are tested, and sampled standard-format files are readable. Transfer descriptions and access responsibilities are undefined. Funding permits one immediate improvement before acceptance. Which investment best closes the most consequential demonstrated gap?
choices: Convert the readable files into a second standard format before defining custody
Agree minimum transfer descriptions, accountable custody, and a tested retrieval handoff
Purchase additional storage replicas before accepting any transfer documentation
Implement a comprehensive description schema before agreeing who accepts and supplies records
rationale: The immediate gap is the archive's ability to accept, describe, account for, and supply the collection. Minimum agreed descriptions and accountable handoffs address it before transfer. More replicas or additional conversion target risks already controlled; a comprehensive schema can delay the essential operational agreement without resolving responsibility.

stem: A hospital system inventory lists an imaging platform, the information inventory lists diagnostic images, and interviews reveal that clinicians export images into a separate referral portal. What should the inventory team do before declaring coverage complete?
choices: Trace the referral process to identify additional holdings, owners, and controls
Record only the partner contract because outsourced holdings are governed outside the inventory
Complete the systems list now and defer analysis of information handoffs until an incident
Treat the referral export as a duplicate once the source platform has been inventoried
rationale: Process tracing reveals additional holdings and their management responsibilities. An export may differ in context, use, or controls even when its source is known. A contract is important but does not inventory the information. Deferring handoff analysis leaves a known coverage gap and undermines the claim of complete inventory.

stem: Customer service agents find three conflicting copies of contact preferences and use whichever appears first. Privacy staff receive complaints about unwanted messages. Which information management improvement best addresses the underlying cause?
choices: Centralize the copies in one folder while preserving their separate update routines
Ask agents to compare the three copies manually before sending each message
Adopt the most recently modified file as authoritative without validating change provenance
Set authoritative preferences and propagate controlled changes to dependent processes
rationale: Authoritative preferences with controlled updates resolve the inconsistent inputs to messaging. Manual comparison leaves repeated interpretation and errors. A recent modification can be a technical change rather than the latest valid preference. Central storage alone does not establish authority or reconcile separate routines that continue producing conflicting copies.

stem: A taxonomy design group includes records specialists and software engineers. It has not tested whether proposed categories reflect how operational staff distinguish cases. Which addition most directly addresses the current design risk?
choices: Additional infrastructure engineers responsible for repository availability
Representative operational users and subject experts from affected functions
An external designer instructed to reproduce the current category names
A procurement specialist focused on the software supplier's contract terms
rationale: Business users and subject experts validate domain meaning and usability, complementing information architecture and technical implementation expertise. More infrastructure or procurement expertise addresses different concerns. An external designer may help, but reproducing existing names without business validation does not resolve the specific risk described.

stem: An analyst shadows an experienced clerk, who follows every documented step while being observed. Transaction records indicate frequent deviations across the team. Which next action best improves confidence in the description of actual work?
choices: Accept the observed sequence because direct observation is conclusive
Discard the records because the experienced clerk is more credible
Interview the clerk again without reviewing any other work evidence
Compare records with interviews and observations across representative staff
rationale: Observation can change behavior, and one experienced clerk may not represent the team. Combining records, interviews, and representative observations tests whether the apparent sequence reflects normal practice. Treating observation as conclusive or discarding contrary records ignores evidence. Repeating only the same interview does not address the sampling limitation.

stem: A recently merged organization has one division that shares information freely and another that requires managerial permission for routine internal access. Before designing the combined IM program, what should the baseline organizational assessment capture?
choices: The preferred vendor interface selected by the largest division
The total storage capacity without examining work or culture
Their different behaviors, decision practices and underlying reasons
A single average maturity score that conceals divisional differences
rationale: The assessment needs to understand operating practices and culture as well as formal requirements. Different access behaviors may reflect legitimate needs or habits requiring change. Storage capacity alone is a technical measure. A concealed average loses actionable differences, while selecting a preferred interface is not a baseline assessment.

stem: Every case needs ten minutes of specialist assessment and five minutes of release review by the same qualified team. That team has 600 minutes daily; other stages support eighty cases daily. A proposal treats assessment and release as independent capacities of sixty and 120 cases. What planning correction is required?
choices: Combine both demands: the shared team can sustain forty cases daily
Use ninety daily by averaging the separately calculated specialist capacities
Use eighty daily because the surrounding stages limit the wider process
Use sixty daily because assessment is the slower of the two specialist activities
rationale: The two activities consume the same constrained resource, so each case requires fifteen specialist minutes. Six hundred divided by fifteen gives forty daily. Sixty assumes release has separate capacity; eighty ignores the specialist constraint. Averaging hypothetical capacities has no basis when both tasks must draw from the same finite pool.

stem: A supported repository version can meet the new requirements, but a custom connector depends on an older database release scheduled for retirement. What should the technical assessment establish before recommending continued use of the repository?
choices: The repository license renewal price without including changes to its dependent components
The repository feature fit and user satisfaction with its current screens
The connector dependency, supported upgrade path, and operational impact
The vendor’s standard API roadmap without examining the custom connector implementation
rationale: The connector and retiring database can constrain an otherwise suitable repository, so their upgrade path and operational impacts must be assessed. Feature fit and user satisfaction do not resolve compatibility. A standard API roadmap may not cover the custom integration, and license price alone omits the changes needed to keep the solution operating.

stem: Counsel confirms that a dataset must be kept at least six years under one applicable rule and erased after four under another unless a documented exemption applies. The organization has not assessed exemptions. How should retention be set?
choices: Keep a six-year archival copy while deleting the operational copy at four years
Apply four years because a deletion deadline automatically overrides all retention minima
Resolve applicability and exemptions with counsel before configuring an authorized rule
Apply six years because a minimum preservation requirement automatically overrides a deletion maximum
rationale: The stated rules conflict unless applicability or an exemption resolves them. Neither a generic preference for retention nor one for deletion settles that legal issue. Keeping an archival copy may still violate the maximum if the rule covers retained information regardless of location. Counsel must establish the authorized treatment.

stem: During review, counsel finds messages referring to a previously unknown project alias and a second decision maker outside the original date range. The original collection followed its approved scope correctly. What is the most defensible next step?
choices: Repeat the original search unchanged to demonstrate that it is reproducible
Reassess scope with counsel and identify additional sources and preservation needs
Remove the messages because they do not match the original search terms
Complete production using the original scope because collection was properly approved
rationale: Analysis can reveal additional people, timeframes, or sources and require returning to identification and preservation. An approved initial scope does not justify ignoring new relevant evidence. Removing the messages suppresses potentially responsive content, while repeating the old search unchanged adds reproducibility without addressing the newly discovered gap.

stem: Caseworkers know the new capture procedure, but their closure bonus ignores completeness. Audits show missing evidence mainly during target-setting weeks. Management can change performance measures next month; system redesign would take six months. Which intervention is most likely to improve adoption promptly and sustainably?
choices: Commission the redesign and suspend all change-management activity until the system changes
Align closure rewards and managerial review with complete evidence, supported by targeted coaching
Add a monthly completeness audit while preserving the incentives that drive weekly behavior
Repeat mandatory navigation training and retain the existing closure-based bonus measures
rationale: The timing and training evidence point to incentives as the main cause. Adjusting rewards and managerial review addresses it within the available timeframe, with coaching reinforcing expectations. Navigation training targets a skill gap not demonstrated here. Audits identify failures but preserve the incentive; waiting for redesign leaves an actionable cause untouched.

stem: A consultancy must update biographies for everyone who contributed to a completed program. Searching document text misses contributors whose biographies do not mention the program. Which metadata would best support the required batch retrieval?
choices: The name of the application used to create each biography
The date each biography was last opened by a reader
A maintained relationship between each person and their program assignments
The number of words currently contained in each biography
rationale: Program-assignment metadata directly identifies the population needing updates even when that relationship is absent from document text. Last-opened dates measure use, authoring applications describe technical origin, and word counts describe size. None establishes which people contributed to the program and therefore require coordinated updates.

stem: Analysts develop lengthy assessment reports on personal computers. Several unfinished reports are lost when a device fails, although published reports are archived reliably. Which change best addresses the exposed capture point?
